vulnerability: R7 exclusive session claims prevent duplicate identity but allow separate development processes to own different session claims within same directory; owner-exclusive scientific custody would require a single journal-level write attempt

design.create: O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY with durable file fsync and POSIX parent dir fsync when possible; marker never deleted or rewritten
design.before_session: claim marker before any individual session claim, no source effects
design.cold_open: if marker preexists, parse canonical bytes and check schema/run/scope identity; reopen always READ_ONLY even same run; never grants new claim or append
design.concurrency: two concurrent journal initializations for same directory permit at most one write owner; loser is read-only; no multi-process write sharing
design.cross_run: different DEV-RUN id can inspect status only, cannot mutate
design.claim_consistency: claim.run_id must equal marker.run_id; unknown claim filename or malformed contents fail closed when advancing phase
design.crash: failed marker fsync may leave an irreversible used marker; subsequent open must not write; corrupted marker fails closed
design.platform: POSIX file+directory fsync test; Windows file fsync only and explicitly not production owner directory guarantee
design.claim_budget: original 480 sessions and 46080 max fictional effects, 96 reserved per claim, first-use always denied

negative_tests: two concurrent owners different intended sessions at same temp directory exactly one writer
fault-injected fsync during owner marker makes all future mutation impossible
forged claim run-id cannot pass audit
fabricated source receipts never imply authority
